# Gap analysis: motion-continuous local video generation

As of 2026-08-01. No files were edited.

## Executive conclusion

No open system currently satisfies all four requirements as a proven turnkey path:

1. Accept a multi-frame or latent tail from the previous generated clip.
2. Simultaneously target a future still keyframe.
3. Preserve smoke/liquid/angular velocity through the join.
4. Run reliably in ComfyUI on a 36GB Apple-Silicon Mac.

The strongest candidates are:

1. **LTX-2.3** — best architecture to benchmark locally. ComfyUI can place image/video guides at arbitrary times, including a previous tail and future still. It has current upstream MPS support and Apple-native MLX ports with Q4/Q8 block streaming. The gap is that no primary source demonstrates this exact dual-conditioned chain on 36GB, and official ComfyUI documentation still specifies CUDA with 32GB+ VRAM.
2. **Wan SVI2Pro-FLF** — closest task-specific implementation. It consumes a previous latent tail and hard-locks end latents. However, it is an experimental community composition, not a model trained jointly for these constraints; its own README documents end-slot conflict, ghosting, and trimming workarounds. Wan 2.2 A14B is a poor fit for 36GB MPS.
3. **VACE 1.3B** — most plausible lightweight control. VACE natively supports first/last clips and arbitrary masked control-video slots, so a prior tail plus end still is expressible. Quality is substantially below 14B and the motion can become linear or endpoint-dominated. MPS feasibility is plausible through native ComfyUI, but not validated by the official CUDA implementation.
4. **SkyReels-V2 DF** — excellent native continuation design, but its official code exposes video extension and first/last-frame generation in mutually exclusive branches/pipeline classes. It is also hard-coded to CUDA and requires FlashAttention.
5. **FramePack** — F1 preserves history but cannot target an end frame; the original bidirectional model can do both only through unmerged community modifications, with weaker motion continuation.
6. **HunyuanVideo, CogVideoX, LongCat, OmniWeaving** — useful comparison systems, but do not provide a proven, Mac-feasible version of the exact dual condition.

The most defensible recommendation is therefore:

- Benchmark **LTX-2.3 Q4/Q8 MLX or upstream MPS streaming** first.
- Include **VACE 1.3B** as the low-memory trained-control baseline.
- Include **Wan SVI2Pro-FLF** only as an experimental upper-quality candidate.
- Treat SkyReels, FramePack-F1, CogVideoX, Hunyuan, and LongCat as ablations demonstrating which half of the requirement they solve.

---

## Capability classification

### A. Systems that can express prior temporal context plus a future keyframe

#### LTX-Video / LTX-2.3

This is the strongest general solution.

Official legacy LTX-Video states that it supports:

> “image-to-video, multi-keyframe conditioning, keyframe-based animation, video extension (both forward and backward), video-to-video transformations, and any combination of these features.”

Source: [Lightricks/LTX-Video](https://github.com/Lightricks/LTX-Video)

Current ComfyUI’s `LTXVAddGuide` accepts either an image or video, places it at a chosen frame index, and supports multiple chained guides:

> “The LTXVAddGuide node adds video conditioning guidance … by encoding input images or videos and incorporating them as keyframes.”

A previous 9/17/25-frame tail can therefore be placed at frame 0 and a target still at the final valid position. Video guides of nine or more frames must start on a multiple of eight.

Sources:

- [LTXVAddGuide documentation](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/embedded-docs/blob/main/comfyui_embedded_docs/docs/LTXVAddGuide/en.md)
- [Merged LTX-2 context-window support](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/pull/13325)
- [LTX-2 keyframe pipeline](https://github.com/Lightricks/LTX-2/blob/main/packages/ltx-pipelines/src/ltx_pipelines/keyframe_interpolation.py)

The merged ComfyUI work explicitly supports:

- Context-window generation.
- Guides at arbitrary positions.
- Multi-frame guide alignment.
- First/last-frame workflows.
- Retention of inplace-conditioned latents across windows.

Important caveats:

- LTX-2’s official keyframe pipeline uses **additive guiding latents**, not exact replacement, so endpoint fidelity is not guaranteed.
- The exact combination “clean previous tail + future still” is supported by the generic guide interface but not demonstrated in an official benchmark.
- LTX’s eight-frame latent stride means endpoint placement and overlap must align carefully.
- Generating a full joined window around the boundary is more defensible than repeatedly decoding and re-encoding a last frame.

#### Wan SVI2Pro-FLF

SVI 2.0 Pro itself is genuinely trained for latent-history conditioning. Its official design is:

> “the first-frame latent … the last latent from the previous clip … followed by zero-value latents.”

It explicitly avoids decoding/re-encoding the prior last frame:

> “We will never use the decoded last frame from the previous clip to generate the current clip.”

Source: [SVI 2.0 Pro design](https://github.com/vita-epfl/Stable-Video-Infinity/blob/svi_wan22/docs/svi/svi_2.0_pro.md)

The community FLF node adds:

- `prev_samples`: last one or two latent slots from the prior segment.
- `anchor_samples`: start image or clip.
- `end_samples`: hard-locked final latent slots.

Source: [ComfyUI-Wan-SVI2Pro-FLF](https://github.com/Well-Made/ComfyUI-Wan-SVI2Pro-FLF)

This is the most direct match to the requested graph, but it is not a jointly trained capability. The node documents several serious traps:

- Hard end slots and SVI steering “can clash and produce heavy artifacts.”
- Its recommended solution is to drop the hard-locked final slot before feeding history to the next segment.
- VAE splitting can cause seam ghosting or doubling.
- The author calls the trimming strategy:

> “a pragmatic workaround, not a theoretical limitation.”

The official SVI tracker also warned that its earlier end-frame support:

> “cannot support large difference between the first and last frame.”

Sources:

- [SVI community variants](https://github.com/vita-epfl/Stable-Video-Infinity/issues/51)
- [Open SVI end-frame issue](https://github.com/vita-epfl/Stable-Video-Infinity/issues/89)

Thus “deterministic endpoint” in the custom-node README should not be interpreted as proven trajectory quality.

#### Wan VACE

VACE is trained for masked video completion and composable references. Its official user guide supports:

- `firstframe`, `lastframe`, `firstlastframe`
- `firstclip`, `lastclip`, `firstlastclip`

Source: [VACE User Guide](https://github.com/ali-vilab/VACE/blob/main/UserGuide.md)

A prior motion tail can be placed in the first control slots, unknown middle slots masked gray, and the future still or short target clip placed at the end. This is a better-trained formulation than the SVI hard-lock hack.

ComfyUI has native `WanVaceToVideo` support for arbitrary control video and masks:

- [WanVaceToVideo documentation](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/embedded-docs/blob/main/comfyui_embedded_docs/docs/WanVaceToVideo/en.md)
- [Official VACE repository](https://github.com/ali-vilab/VACE)

Caveats:

- Frame counts must be `4n+1`.
- A still target should be encoded consistently with the control mask; duplicating it into a short final clip may improve endpoint influence but adds an artificial zero-velocity condition.
- The 1.3B model is the realistic Mac candidate, but likely loses turbulent detail and complex motion.
- Community reports describe VACE multi-keyframe motion as comparatively linear; this is not quantified by the official paper.

### B. Systems with both capabilities, but not simultaneously in the official path

#### SkyReels-V2 Diffusion Forcing

SkyReels has excellent native history conditioning:

> “extend video generation indefinitely based on the last frames of the previous segment.”

It recommends a 17-frame overlap.

Source: [SkyReels-V2](https://github.com/SkyworkAI/SkyReels-V2)

It separately supports first/last-frame generation. However, the official `generate_video_df.py` does:

- If `video_path` exists: call `extend_video(...)`.
- Else: call the image pipeline with `image` and `end_image`.

The extension call does not pass `end_image`.

Source: [generate_video_df.py](https://github.com/SkyworkAI/SkyReels-V2/blob/main/generate_video_df.py)

Diffusers similarly exposes distinct video-to-video and first/last image pipeline classes:

- [SkyReels-V2 Diffusers documentation](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/blob/main/docs/source/en/api/pipelines/skyreels_v2.md)

Therefore, claims that stock SkyReels simultaneously consumes a previous clip and future endpoint are unsupported. Diffusion Forcing should theoretically allow arbitrary clean tokens, but no primary source provides that implementation.

#### CogVideoX

The official CLI supports separate T2V, I2V, and V2V pipelines:

- [CogVideoX CLI](https://github.com/THUDM/CogVideo/blob/main/inference/cli_demo.py)
- [CogVideo repository](https://github.com/THUDM/CogVideo)

A separate finetuned model implements keyframe interpolation:

- [CogVideoX-Interpolation](https://github.com/feizc/CogvideX-Interpolation)

There is no official pipeline combining V2V continuation context with interpolation endpoint control. The ComfyUI wrapper advertises both temporal tiling and interpolation, but no primary test establishes their simultaneous use.

### C. History-only or endpoint-only systems

#### FramePack / FramePack-F1

Official F1:

> “only predicts future frames from history frames.”

Source: [FramePack-F1 announcement](https://github.com/lllyasviel/FramePack/discussions/459)

That is useful for velocity retention, but F1 does not support end latents in the main ComfyUI wrapper. The original bidirectional model has community end-frame and video-input patches, but the key PR states:

> “it only works with the original backward generation model — I haven't been able to get it working with F1.”

It also says F1 is better at maintaining input motion.

Sources:

- [Video input plus end-frame PR](https://github.com/lllyasviel/FramePack/pull/491)
- [Start/end-frame PR](https://github.com/lllyasviel/FramePack/pull/167)
- [ComfyUI FramePack wrapper](https://github.com/kijai/ComfyUI-FramePackWrapper)

Thus FramePack currently forces a choice:

- F1: stronger continuation, no endpoint.
- Original: experimental endpoint, weaker continuation.

#### HunyuanVideo

Base HunyuanVideo-I2V is a first-frame model, not a continuation-plus-endpoint system:

- [HunyuanVideo-I2V](https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/HunyuanVideo-I2V)

The Hunyuan-derived FramePack pipeline supports first and last images but not an arbitrary external history tail in its standard interface:

- [Diffusers FramePack pipeline](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/blob/main/src/diffusers/pipelines/hunyuan_video/pipeline_hunyuan_video_framepack.py)

Newer **OmniWeaving** adds interpolation, video editing, and text-image-video-to-video tasks:

- [OmniWeaving](https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/OmniWeaving)

However, interpolation and TIV2V remain separate task flags. There is no evidence that the image in TIV2V is interpreted as a future endpoint while the video supplies prior motion.

#### LongCat-Video

LongCat is natively trained for continuation:

> “natively pretrained on Video-Continuation tasks.”

Source: [LongCat-Video](https://github.com/meituan-longcat/LongCat-Video)

It has no documented terminal keyframe control. Its “minutes-long without color drifting” statement is a first-party claim, not an independent result.

---

## Apple Silicon / 36GB feasibility

### General traps

A 36GB Mac does not provide 36GB of independent GPU VRAM. ComfyUI identifies MPS as `VRAMState.SHARED`; model weights, activations, text encoders, macOS, and CPU offload all consume the same unified pool.

Source: [ComfyUI MPS placement fix](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/commit/c00d1d7a741884a212c68312bfd471c46b086e50)

Consequences:

- CUDA “CPU offload” numbers do not transfer directly. Offloading can reduce MPS residency but does not create additional physical RAM.
- Keep roughly 6–10GB for macOS and working allocations.
- `PYTORCH_MPS_HIGH_WATERMARK_RATIO=0.0` may avoid allocator limits but can destabilize or kill the whole system.
- Apple describes MPS support as beta: [Apple MPS documentation](https://developer.apple.com/metal/pytorch/).

FP8 remains unsupported in native PyTorch MPS:

- [PyTorch float8 MPS issue](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/132624)
- [ComfyUI FP8 MPS failure](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/issues/9255)

Community Metal FP8 kernels exist, but they are not equivalent to tested CUDA FP8 paths and should be a separate benchmark configuration.

### Per-system feasibility

#### LTX-Video legacy

- Officially tested with MPS.
- Official source says PyTorch 2.3 or 2.6+.
- No mandatory FlashAttention.
- Legacy 2B is the safest high-control baseline on 36GB.
- CUDA Q8 kernels target NVIDIA Ada and do not help MPS.
- A 13B checkpoint plus large T5 encoder is tight unless integer-quantized and carefully offloaded.

Source: [LTX-Video README](https://github.com/Lightricks/LTX-Video)

Assessment: **feasible at 2B; uncertain at 13B**.

#### LTX-2.3

- 22B BF16 checkpoint is approximately 42–46GB before Gemma 3 12B and activations.
- Official ComfyUI prerequisites still say “CUDA-compatible GPU with 32GB+ VRAM.”
- Official low-VRAM loaders target 32GB CUDA.
- Upstream MPS support was added in July 2026, after a PR demonstrated crashes from unconditional CUDA calls and BF16 STG corruption.
- The validated MPS test used an M5 Max with 128GB, not 36GB.

Sources:

- [LTX-2 MPS PR and upstream response](https://github.com/Lightricks/LTX-2/pull/184)
- [LTX-2 repository](https://github.com/Lightricks/LTX-2)
- [ComfyUI-LTXVideo](https://github.com/Lightricks/ComfyUI-LTXVideo)

Apple-native MLX ports materially change feasibility:

- Q4: approximately 12GB.
- Q8: approximately 21GB.
- BF16: approximately 42GB.
- Block streaming supports Q8 on 16GB and BF16 on 32GB according to the port author.
- Keyframe and extend pipelines are implemented.

Source: [dgrauet/ltx-2-mlx](https://github.com/dgrauet/ltx-2-mlx)

Assessment: **Q4 MLX likely feasible; Q8 tight but plausible; BF16 only with disk streaming and very low resolution**. These figures are community claims, not upstream Lightricks validation.

#### Wan SVI2Pro-FLF / Wan 2.2

Wan 2.2 A14B has 27B total parameters across two experts, with 14B active per denoising phase. “14B active” does not mean only 14B must be stored. The BF16 expert weights alone are roughly 54GB total.

Source: [Wan2.2 model card](https://huggingface.co/Wan-AI/Wan2.2-I2V-A14B)

Other problems:

- Official requirements include `flash_attn`.
- Common Comfy checkpoints are FP8, which MPS cannot natively load.
- Q4/GGUF can lower storage, but dequantization and two-expert switching still require headroom.
- SVI adds LoRAs and latent history on top.

Assessment: **not a reliable 36GB target**. A carefully quantized ComfyUI run may start, but there is no primary-source successful result for this workflow on 36GB MPS.

#### VACE

Official dependencies include:

- `flash_attn`
- `onnxruntime-gpu`
- CUDA-tested PyTorch

Source: [VACE requirements](https://github.com/ali-vilab/VACE/blob/main/requirements/framework.txt)

The official 14B path has required approximately 70GB even with aggressive offload, and users have OOMed on 80–94GB cards:

- [VACE 14B memory issue](https://github.com/ali-vilab/VACE/issues/56)

The 1.3B 480p model is much smaller. SkyReels’ architecturally similar 1.3B path reports 13–14.7GB CUDA peak, suggesting 36GB should be enough if the native Comfy nodes avoid CUDA-only preprocessing. This is an analogy, not a verified VACE MPS measurement.

Assessment: **1.3B probable; 14B no**.

#### SkyReels-V2

Official peaks at 540p:

- DF 1.3B: about 14.7GB CUDA VRAM.
- DF 14B: about 51.2GB.
- I2V 14B: about 43.4GB.

Source: [SkyReels-V2 README](https://github.com/SkyworkAI/SkyReels-V2)

The official path hard-codes:

- `torch.device("cuda")`
- CUDA generator
- `torch.cuda.amp.autocast`
- `torch.cuda.empty_cache`
- NCCL for distributed work

Its requirements include `flash_attn` and `xfuser`.

Assessment: **1.3B could fit in memory after a port, but stock code is not MPS-compatible; 14B is excluded**.

#### FramePack

Official claims six GB minimum NVIDIA VRAM by dynamic model swapping, but explicitly supports NVIDIA RTX and Linux/Windows only.

Source: [FramePack](https://github.com/lllyasviel/FramePack)

Mac forks require attention chunking because MPS attempted contiguous allocations around 15GB. Reports range from:

- Running on 24GB.
- Approximately 190–200 seconds per iteration on an M2 Max 32GB.
- More than an hour for one second under some configurations.

Source: [FramePack Mac support issue](https://github.com/lllyasviel/FramePack/issues/42)

Assessment: **technically possible through community forks, operationally poor, and exact dual control is absent from F1**.

#### HunyuanVideo

Official requirements:

- NVIDIA CUDA.
- 45GB peak for 544×960×129.
- 60GB for 720p.
- I2V 720p: 60GB.

Sources:

- [HunyuanVideo](https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/HunyuanVideo)
- [HunyuanVideo-I2V](https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/HunyuanVideo-I2V)

A reported MPS run requested a 635GB buffer at 720p:

- [MPS buffer issue](https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/HunyuanVideo-I2V/issues/66)

HunyuanVideo-1.5 advertises 14GB with offload, but explicitly requires NVIDIA CUDA. OmniWeaving adds Qwen2.5-VL-7B and defaults to eight inference GPUs.

Assessment: **not suitable**.

#### CogVideoX

Official Diffusers minimum-memory figures use sequential offload and VAE tiling, but MPS attention allocations remain problematic. A 32GB MPS report failed above 16 frames, and a community M4 Pro 64GB setup found roughly 30 frames to be the stable ceiling.

Sources:

- [Diffusers MPS OOM issue](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/issues/9972)
- [CogVideoX Mac setup](https://github.com/nicedreamzapp/CogVideoX-Mac-Setup)

Assessment: **model weights fit, useful sequence lengths often do not**.

#### LongCat / OmniWeaving

LongCat requires FlashAttention 2 by default. A successful CUDA configuration still peaked around 43GB after T5/VAE offload:

- [LongCat 48GB issue](https://github.com/meituan-longcat/LongCat-Video/issues/7)

OmniWeaving uses FlashAttention/Sage/flex-block attention and hard-coded `torch.cuda` initialization.

Assessment: **not feasible on 36GB MPS**.

---

## Recommended benchmark matrix

### Systems

Run these first:

1. LTX-Video legacy 2B, BF16 MPS.
2. LTX-2.3 Q4 MLX low-RAM.
3. LTX-2.3 Q8 MLX low-RAM, if it avoids swap.
4. VACE 1.3B 480p through native ComfyUI.
5. Wan SVI2Pro-FLF Q4/GGUF only if it can complete a smoke test without swap thrashing.

Comparison-only:

6. FramePack-F1, history only.
7. FramePack original plus community video/end-frame fork.
8. SkyReels-V2 DF 1.3B on CUDA or after an explicit port.
9. CogVideoX interpolation and V2V as separate baselines.

### Conditioning ablations

Every capable model should run:

- Last still only.
- One prior frame plus endpoint.
- 9-frame prior tail plus endpoint.
- 17-frame prior tail plus endpoint.
- Prior tail only.
- Endpoint only.
- Prior tail plus deliberately incompatible endpoint.

This separates true velocity retention from endpoint interpolation and hard-lock artifacts.

### Motion cases

Use controlled synthetic or real clips with measurable motion:

1. Laminar smoke translating laterally.
2. Turbulent smoke with persistent vortex.
3. Viscous liquid pour.
4. Water slosh or surface wave.
5. Constant-speed turntable rotation.
6. Accelerating then constant rotation.
7. Camera orbit around a static subject.
8. Articulated cyclic motion for a non-fluid control.

For each, create mild, moderate, and hard endpoint displacement.

### Two evaluation regimes

- **Teacher-forced join:** every model receives the same ground-truth or reference tail and endpoint. This isolates conditional capability.
- **Free-running chain:** each system generates three or five consecutive segments from its own outputs. This measures accumulated drift and latent recycling.

Use at least five matched seeds. Normalize all outputs to the same FPS and metric resolution, but retain native-resolution quality measurements separately.

---

## Boundary metrics

Let the join be between frames \(I_{-1}\) and \(I_0\).

### Motion continuity

1. **Flow magnitude retention**
   - Compute dense flow for pre-join and post-join pairs.
   - Report median post/pre magnitude ratio in the moving region.
   - Detects freezing near the endpoint.

2. **Flow direction discontinuity**
   - Compare cosine angle between advected pre-join flow and join/post-join flow.
   - Report weighted angular error.

3. **Velocity endpoint error**
   - Mean L2 distance between corresponding flow vectors after warping into a common coordinate frame.
   - TC-Bench uses EPE between flow maps: [TC-Bench](https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2406.08656).

4. **Acceleration and jerk discontinuity**
   - First and second temporal differences of flow.
   - Report excess at the boundary relative to median within-segment values.

5. **Warp residual**
   - Warp \(I_{-1}\) toward \(I_0\) using estimated flow.
   - Compute occlusion-masked L1 and LPIPS residual.
   - Large residual with modest flow indicates a visual jump rather than physical motion.

Use RAFT or GMFlow consistently:

- [Official RAFT](https://github.com/princeton-vl/RAFT)
- TC-Bench uses GMFlow-derived EPE.

### Appearance and endpoint control

6. **Normalized seam LPIPS**
   - `LPIPS(I[-1], I[0]) / median within-segment LPIPS`.
   - LPIPS definition: [PerceptualSimilarity](https://github.com/richzhang/PerceptualSimilarity).

7. **DINO feature seam**
   - Cosine distance for global features and moving-region patch features.
   - [DINOv2](https://github.com/facebookresearch/dinov2).

8. **Luminance/chroma jump**
   - Delta mean, standard deviation, and histogram Earth-Mover distance.
   - Important for VAE color drift.

9. **Target endpoint error**
   - LPIPS, SSIM, and DINO distance at the requested final frame.
   - Also report the minimum error in a ±4-frame window to detect early or late arrival.

10. **Endpoint freeze score**
    - Ratio of motion magnitude in the final eight frames to the middle of the segment.
    - Prevents a model from “winning” endpoint accuracy by stopping early.

### Scene-specific kinematics

11. Rotation:
    - Estimate tangential flow around the rotation center.
    - Report angular velocity and phase discontinuity.

12. Smoke/liquid:
    - Segment the moving material.
    - Track centroid, area, optical-flow divergence, curl, and boundary advection.
    - Report continuity across the join.

### Sequence-level metrics

Use VBench’s motion smoothness, dynamic degree, subject consistency, and flicker dimensions as secondary diagnostics:

- [VBench](https://github.com/Vchitect/VBench)

Do not use FVD as the primary join metric. FVD is distribution-level, needs many clips, downsamples to 224×224, and is known to be content-biased and insensitive to temporal defects:

- [Official FVD code](https://github.com/google-research/google-research/tree/master/frechet_video_distance)
- [Content bias in FVD](https://arxiv.org/html/2404.12391v1)

### Runtime telemetry

Record for every run:

- Peak process RSS.
- Peak `torch.mps.driver_allocated_memory()`.
- Peak `torch.mps.current_allocated_memory()`.
- Swap used and memory-pressure events.
- Wall time per generated frame.
- Model-load time.
- Crash/OOM rate.
- Whether CPU fallback occurred.
- Output determinism under a fixed seed.

A generation that “fits” only by entering sustained swap is not operationally feasible.

---

## Claims that should be rejected or heavily qualified

- **“Wan A14B is a 14B model, so BF16 should fit in 36GB.”** False: A14B has about 27B total parameters across two experts.
- **“Six GB FramePack means it fits any six-GB-class system.”** Unsupported for MPS; the figure relies on NVIDIA-oriented swapping and kernels.
- **“SkyReels supports both continuation and end image, therefore it supports them together.”** Not in the official code path.
- **“CPU offload gives a Mac extra memory.”** False on unified memory.
- **“FP8 reduces Wan/LTX memory on MPS.”** Not through native PyTorch MPS.
- **“Hard-locked end latents imply smooth arrival.”** False; SVI2Pro-FLF documents conflicts and crumpled final frames.
- **“Last-frame I2V preserves velocity.”** A still contains no velocity information; any continuity is inferred, not conditioned.
- **“ComfyUI availability implies Apple compatibility.”** Many wrappers call CUDA autocast, CUDA generators, FlashAttention, or unsupported dtypes.
- **“Long-video consistency implies good segment-boundary kinematics.”** Color/identity stability and first-derivative motion continuity are different properties.
- **“FVD measures seam quality.”** It is unsuitable as a primary one-boundary metric.

## Final recommendation

Build the primary review around this hierarchy:

1. **LTX-2.3 guides/context windows** — strongest technical direction and best chance of a native Mac implementation.
2. **VACE 1.3B** — best trained low-memory dual-control baseline.
3. **Wan SVI2Pro-FLF** — exact requested conditioning topology but experimental, memory-risky, and not jointly trained.
4. **SkyReels-V2 DF** — best continuation architecture blocked by separate endpoint API and CUDA.
5. **FramePack-F1** — useful motion-history ablation, not a dual-control answer.

Any document presenting SVI2Pro-FLF as already solved, SkyReels as stock dual-conditioned, or 14B Wan/Hunyuan systems as practical on a 36GB Mac has a material evidence gap.

# Executive conclusion

As of 2026-08-01, there is no production-ready local stack that combines all of these on a 36GB M3 Mac:

1. multiple hard keyframes,
2. genuine multi-frame motion inheritance,
3. high-quality Wan-class output,
4. reliable Apple Silicon acceleration,
5. reasonable render time.

The best technical design is Wan 2.2 + SVI 2.0 Pro latent continuation, augmented with `ComfyUI-Wan-SVI2Pro-FLF` for endpoint control. It carries the previous segment’s native latent tail into the next segment, avoiding decode/re-encode loss. But it requires two 14B Wan 2.2 experts and two SVI LoRAs; full precision does not fit comfortably in 36GB, FP8 is not natively supported by MPS, and quantized ComfyUI operation is slow and fragile.

My concrete recommendation:

1. Best practical local prototype: Wan2.1-VACE-1.3B at 480p, using 8–16 real overlap frames and positioned endpoint references. It fits the Mac much more realistically, but its continuation is control-video/pixel-conditioned rather than native latent continuation.
2. Best local fidelity experiment: Wan 2.2 SVI 2.0 Pro + FLF, quantized to Q2/Q3, 480p, initially 41 frames, `motion_latent_count=1`, SDPA attention, and aggressive sequential unloading. Expect long runtimes and possible MPS incompatibilities.
3. Best paid proof baseline: official hosted Wan 2.7 continuation, with the previous clip as `first_clip` and the next keyframe as optional `last_frame`. This directly tests whether the local methods are losing motion continuity or merely hitting model limits.
4. Best Mac-native engine if strict continuation is relaxed: MLX-Video with Wan 2.2 or LTX-2.3. It is substantially better matched to Apple hardware, but its published interface does not currently expose SVI `prev_samples`, VACE, or LTX keyframe-interpolation pipelines.

“Velocity inheritance” needs one qualification: none of these systems exposes a physical velocity vector. SVI carries a learned temporal latent containing local motion state; VACE and hosted continuation infer velocity from several input frames. SVI is therefore the closest match to the requested property, but not an explicit physics representation.

---

# 1. Wan SVI / SVI 2.0 Pro

## What SVI Pro actually carries forward

**Sourced fact:** SVI 2.0 Pro builds each new conditioning sequence as:

```text
[anchor latent, previous clip motion latent, zero-valued latent padding]

It never decodes the previous last frame and re-encodes it for continuation. This is the central advantage over frame-chaining: no VAE round trip at every segment boundary.

Primary sources:

  • SVI 2.0 Pro design note
  • Exact pipeline implementation
  • Official Wan 2.2 SVI branch
  • SVI paper

The paper reports only a 0.63% subject-consistency drop in its ultra-long evaluation, versus 7.03% for ordinary Wan 2.1 and 13.71% for FramePack. That result is from the authors’ benchmark and hardware, not a guarantee for quantized ComfyUI output.

Exact models and LoRAs

For Wan 2.2 SVI 2.0 Pro:

  • Base model: Wan2.2-I2V-A14B
    • high-noise expert: early denoising/layout/motion
    • low-noise expert: later detail refinement
  • Official SVI Pro high-noise LoRA:
    • SVI_Wan2.2-I2V-A14B_high_noise_lora_v2.0_pro.safetensors
  • Official SVI Pro low-noise LoRA:
    • SVI_Wan2.2-I2V-A14B_low_noise_lora_v2.0_pro.safetensors
  • Official model directory:
    • vita-video-gen/svi-model/version-2.0
  • Comfy-native converted versions:
    • SVI_v2_PRO_Wan2.2-I2V-A14B_HIGH_lora_rank_128_fp16.safetensors
    • SVI_v2_PRO_Wan2.2-I2V-A14B_LOW_lora_rank_128_fp16.safetensors
    • Kijai converted SVI directory

Load each SVI LoRA only into its matching high- or low-noise expert.

For Wan 2.1:

  • SVI_Wan2.1-I2V-14B_lora_v2.0.safetensors
  • This is SVI 2.0, not the same latent-continuation Pro architecture.
  • The authors explicitly warn that it cannot use an ordinary Wan 2.1 workflow because it needs modified padding.

Official baseline settings

The official Wan 2.2 example uses:

  • 832×480
  • 81 frames per clip
  • 15 fps
  • num_motion_latent=1
  • num_overlap_frame=5
  • different seed per clip
  • 50 clips in the published long-run command

Source: SVI Wan 2.2 README.

The official script uses:

seed = clip_idx * seed_multiplier
prev_last_latent = generated latent tail
next clip = video_frames[num_overlap_frame:]

Source: inference_svi_2.0_pro.py.

prev_samples and motion_latent_count

In the Comfy implementation:

  • prev_samples must be the sampler’s native output latent, shaped [B,C,T,H,W].
  • motion_latent_count=1 copies its final temporal slot.
  • motion_latent_count=2 copies two temporal slots.
  • 0 disables temporal continuation.

Because Wan has temporal stride 4, one latent slot spans approximately four new frames, with boundary accounting making the practical overlap five decoded frames.

Recommendation: start with 1. It is the official Pro setting and leaves the model more freedom to reach the next keyframe. Test 2 only for rapid or strongly directional motion; it can preserve more local trajectory but may also echo poses, overconstrain the beginning, or fight endpoint guidance.

Never decode and re-encode the previous clip to construct prev_samples; that removes the main benefit of SVI Pro.

2. ComfyUI-Wan-SVI2Pro-FLF

Repository: Well-Made/ComfyUI-Wan-SVI2Pro-FLF

Exact nodes

The package adds:

  • WanImageToVideoSVIProFLF
    • category: conditioning/video_models
  • WanCutLastSlot
    • category: latent/video

Its supplied workflows use either:

  • KSampler (Advanced), or
  • SamplerCustomAdvanced

and use Image Batch Extend With Overlap for decoded-frame assembly.

The normal upstream node is:

  • WanImageToVideoSVIPro

from ComfyUI-KJNodes, with anchor_samples, optional prev_samples, and motion_latent_count.

For model loading, retain the official native Wan 2.2 I2V dual-expert template and load the SVI high/low LoRAs into their corresponding experts. The FLF node replaces the ordinary image-to-video conditioning stage; it does not replace Wan’s high/low sampler architecture.

Endpoint handling

The FLF node constructs:

anchor_samples
+ last motion_latent_count slots from prev_samples
+ Wan-format zero padding

It then overwrites the final temporal slots with end_samples and sets those slots to zero in concat_mask. In this mask convention, zero means the corresponding conditioning latent is hard-locked.

Source code: nodes.py.

This is an experimental composition of two independently useful mechanisms:

  • SVI motion continuation at the start;
  • FLF hard endpoint control at the end.

It is not an officially trained SVI endpoint mode.

Why the last-slot cut exists

A hard endpoint can conflict with SVI’s learned motion trajectory. The repository documents “crumpled” or heavily distorted frames when the final hard-locked latent is fed back as the next clip’s motion context.

The recommended workaround is:

generated latent
  ├─ decode full latent for output
  └─ WanCutLastSlot(slots_to_cut=1) → next segment prev_samples

This preserves the visible endpoint in the assembled video but prevents the exact hard-locked terminal slot from steering the next generation.

Recommendation: use this split-path design. Do not trim the only copy before decoding.

Repository caveats

The node is useful, but not yet production-hardened:

  • Its schema declares prev_samples as required although the implementation and README describe it as optional for the first segment.
  • VAE chunk boundaries can vary enough that the repository recommends adjusting decoded overlap by one or two frames.
  • The author says compatibility with arbitrary model combinations is not exhaustively tested.
  • The repository notes washed-out output and includes a contrast-adjustment workaround.
  • Its endpoint mechanism can reduce prompt adherence when the segment is too short.

These are reasons to treat FLF as an experiment requiring QA, not a drop-in deterministic animation solver.

3. Recommended SVI multi-keyframe graph

Given keyframes K0 … Kn:

Segment 0

  • anchor_samples = VAE(K0)
  • end_samples = VAE(K1)
  • no meaningful previous latent
  • motion_latent_count = 0
  • generate 81 frames initially

Because of the current required-input declaration, the provided workflow may need an anchor/repeated latent connected to prev_samples, or the first segment may use ordinary FLF conditioning before switching to the SVI-FLF node.

Segment i > 0

  • anchor_samples = VAE(Ki)
  • prev_samples = WanCutLastSlot(previous raw generated latent, 1)
  • end_samples = VAE(Ki+1)
  • motion_latent_count = 1
  • use a new seed
  • keep subject/style text stable while changing only action and camera direction

Stitching

  • Keep all frames from segment 0.
  • Remove the first five decoded frames from each subsequent segment, matching the official SVI configuration.
  • If ghosting remains, test 4, 5, and 6—not arbitrary large overlaps.
  • Prefer a hard overlap removal over a long dissolve. Crossfades often create double limbs and reduce apparent velocity.
  • If a blend is necessary, align the overlap with optical flow first and blend only one or two frames.

The FLF repository’s adjustable overlap addresses VAE boundary variation. The official SVI five-frame trim remains the principled starting point.

Segment duration

Use 81 frames for initial tests. The FLF author reports that 81–101 frames can improve prompt adherence because the beginning is occupied with continuing previous motion and the end is occupied with endpoint convergence.

For hard keyframes that imply a major pose or camera change, give the model more temporal room rather than increasing endpoint strength.

4. Wan 2.1 VACE continuation

Primary implementation: ali-vilab/VACE

Official variants

  • Wan2.1-VACE-1.3B
    • approximately 81×480×832
  • Wan2.1-VACE-14B
    • approximately 81×720×1280
  • VACE-LTX-Video-0.9
    • approximately 97×512×768

The official code was tested with CUDA 12.4 and PyTorch 2.5.1. It does not claim native MPS support.

How VACE continuation works

VACE accepts:

  • src_video
  • src_mask
  • reference images
  • prompt

For temporal continuation, a source/control video shorter than the requested output is treated as temporal outpainting. Sliding-window implementations preserve overlap from the previous window and generate the remainder.

Useful control representation:

  • black mask: preserve
  • white mask: process
  • grey value 127 in the control video: regenerate/inpaint
  • positioned reference images: force a particular image near a chosen frame

Source:

  • VACE README
  • VACE User Guide
  • Wan2GP VACE guide
  • Wan2GP temporal-processing guide

Practical multi-keyframe recipe

For each segment:

  1. Carry the final 8–16 real frames from the previous segment into the new control video.
  2. Mark those frames “keep unchanged.”
  3. Fill the future region with VACE’s regeneration/inpainting representation.
  4. Position the next keyframe at the final desired frame.
  5. Generate only a short window.
  6. Remove the duplicated overlap from the output.
  7. Persist each completed segment to disk before starting the next.

The contiguous overlap provides enough observations for VACE to infer direction and approximate speed. It is more informative than last-frame chaining but still incurs VAE/control conditioning and may alter the preserved area slightly.

Memory variants and optimization

Recommendation for this Mac: start with the 1.3B model at 480p. It is the only official VACE variant with a realistic memory margin.

For 14B:

  • quantization is effectively mandatory;
  • block swapping on a Mac does not create more physical memory because CPU and GPU share the same unified pool;
  • it may reduce MPS-private allocations, but every copied/offloaded block still occupies the same 36GB and adds synchronization overhead.

Disk-backed segment storage and incremental assembly prevent long videos from filling RAM. Community implementations such as wan-video-extender and ComfyUI_vaceFramepack offer such mechanisms, but their “arbitrary length” and semantic-memory selectors are community additions, not official VACE guarantees.

VACE is the more practical Mac choice; SVI Pro remains the cleaner motion-continuation architecture.

5. Hosted Wan 2.7 baseline

As of the access date, I found official hosted Wan 2.7 APIs but no official downloadable Wan 2.7 weights or local inference repository. Treat claims that Wan 2.7 is currently open-weight/local as unverified unless Alibaba publishes those assets.

Official model: wan2.7-i2v-2026-04-25

The API supports:

  • first-frame-to-video;
  • first-and-last-frame-to-video;
  • video continuation;
  • first_clip plus optional last_frame;
  • 720p or 1080p;
  • total duration 2–15 seconds.

In continuation mode, the returned video includes the original input clip. If a two-second source is submitted with duration 12, the result is two seconds of original footage plus ten generated seconds.

Primary sources:

  • Wan 2.7 I2V API
  • Wan 2.7 I2V guide
  • Alibaba Model Studio pricing

International pricing on 2026-08-01:

  • 720p: $0.10 per output second
  • 1080p: $0.15 per output second
  • initial 50-second quota listed by Alibaba
  • failed requests are not billed
  • input is free, but continuation’s returned total duration includes the input clip

Thus a 12-second continuation containing a two-second input is billed for 12 seconds, not only the ten generated seconds.

fal.ai also lists $0.10/output-second for its Wan 2.7 endpoints: fal Wan 2.7.

Baseline protocol

For every difficult local segment:

  1. Submit the local previous clip, not merely its last frame.
  2. Supply the same target endpoint as last_frame.
  3. Use the same action/camera prompt.
  4. Compare:
    • seam velocity;
    • endpoint adherence;
    • identity retention;
    • prompt compliance;
    • motion amplitude.

If Wan 2.7 succeeds and local VACE/SVI fails, the problem is likely local model capacity or quantization. If Wan 2.7 also fails, the keyframe transition itself may be underdetermined or physically implausible.

6. Other local and long-video systems

LTX-Video / LTX-2 / LTX-2.3

Official code: Lightricks/LTX-2

Current LTX-2.3 provides:

  • 22B dev and distilled models;
  • synchronized audio/video;
  • KeyframeInterpolationPipeline;
  • image-to-video;
  • video-to-video via IC-LoRA;
  • retake of a selected temporal region;
  • an eight-step distilled pipeline;
  • CPU/disk offload;
  • FP8 quantization.

This is arguably the strongest open multi-keyframe toolkit by feature breadth. But the official acceleration path targets CUDA, FlashAttention 3/4, and FP8. A 22B BF16 transformer alone is around 44GB before text encoder, VAE, audio model, and activations.

The official Comfy package is Lightricks/ComfyUI-LTXVideo. Open issues document CUDA prerequisites and MPS failures.

Mac-native alternatives exist:

  • Blaizzy/mlx-video
  • dgrauet/ltx-2-mlx

These support quantized LTX-2.3 T2V/I2V/A2V much more naturally on Apple Silicon. However, their documented interfaces do not currently expose the official keyframe interpolation, retake, or native continuation pipelines. Therefore LTX is promising but does not presently beat SVI/VACE for this exact local task.

FramePack / FramePack-F1

Official repository: lllyasviel/FramePack

Strengths:

  • genuine next-section prediction;
  • constant-length packed context;
  • workload approximately invariant with video duration;
  • F1 predicts only forward from history and has greater dynamics;
  • official claim: 13B model can generate one minute using 6GB NVIDIA VRAM.

Limits:

  • officially requires NVIDIA RTX, Linux or Windows;
  • no official macOS/MPS support;
  • not designed around arbitrary hard intermediate keyframes;
  • TeaCache, quantization, and alternate attention can materially change results;
  • its 1.5–2.5 seconds/frame figures are RTX 4090 figures, not Mac estimates.

FramePack is an excellent long free-running motion model but not a viable official M3 method and not a deterministic keyframe path solver.

SkyReels-V2 Diffusion Forcing

Official repository: SkyworkAI/SkyReels-V2

This is a true autoregressive/diffusion-forcing long-video system:

  • continuation from preceding frames;
  • video extension;
  • start/end frame control;
  • synchronous and asynchronous modes;
  • cleaner earlier blocks condition noisier later blocks.

Official peak figures:

  • 1.3B 540p: approximately 14.7GB
  • 14B 540p: approximately 51.2GB
  • ordinary 14B I2V path: approximately 43.4GB

The inference code moves pipelines to CUDA explicitly. It is theoretically small enough in its 1.3B form, but not a supported MPS solution.

SkyReels-V3

Official repository: SkyworkAI/SkyReels-V3

This supersedes V2 for several production uses:

  • dedicated 14B 720p video-extension model;
  • single-shot continuation from 5–30 seconds;
  • shot-switching continuation;
  • reference-to-video;
  • FP8 weight-only low-VRAM mode plus block offload.

It recommends CUDA 12.8. Its low-VRAM path depends on FP8 and block offload, making it unsuitable for this Mac despite being one of the stronger current open continuation systems.

HunyuanVideo

Original HunyuanVideo requires NVIDIA CUDA and officially lists roughly 45–60GB minimum depending on output size: Tencent-Hunyuan/HunyuanVideo.

HunyuanVideo-1.5 is much more efficient:

  • 8.3B parameters;
  • T2V and I2V;
  • 480p distilled I2V at 8 or 12 steps;
  • 13.6GB peak for 720p/121 frames in the authors’ CUDA pipeline with pipeline/group offload and VAE tiling.

It still lacks native arbitrary multi-keyframe continuation. Last-frame chaining discards velocity, so it is not a preferred solution here.

CogVideoX

Official repository: zai-org/CogVideo

CogVideoX offers:

  • 2B and 5B variants;
  • sequential CPU offload;
  • INT8/FP8 examples;
  • DDIM inversion;
  • a separate CogVideoX-Interpolation project.

It is lighter and older, but neither its mainline model nor the interpolation fork offers a better combination of motion continuation, keyframe control, quality, and Apple support than VACE or LTX.

LongCat-Video

Official repository: meituan-longcat/LongCat-Video

This is a serious current alternative:

  • 13.6B;
  • native T2V, I2V, and video continuation in one model;
  • trained for minute-long continuation;
  • claims no color drift or quality degradation;
  • explicit run_demo_video_continuation.py and long-video scripts.

Its official stack requires CUDA, FlashAttention, and usually torch.compile; it is not a Mac solution.

Newer research-only systems

  • NVIDIA LongLive: native long-video autoregression with KV recaching and frame sinks, up to 240 seconds. Official requirement is Linux/NVIDIA with at least 40GB.
  • Helios/Open-Sora-Plan: minute-scale long generation at 19.5 FPS on one H100, not a Mac implementation.
  • LongLive 2.0: stronger 5B long generation using NVFP4 and Blackwell-specific infrastructure, fundamentally unavailable on M3.
  • DreaMontage paper: arbitrary-frame and multi-keyframe conditioning is highly relevant, but it is presently a research result rather than a mature local Mac workflow.

7. Apple Silicon reality

MPS

PyTorch’s MPS backend provides GPU access through Metal and shares unified memory with the CPU:

  • PyTorch MPS documentation
  • PyTorch Apple Silicon architecture overview

Unified memory avoids PCIe copies but does not make all 36GB safely available to a model. macOS, display buffers, Python, ComfyUI, decoded frames, model weights, activations, and temporary VAE tensors share it.

FP8

MPS does not natively support the FP8 workflow assumed by many Wan and LTX templates. A documented Wan 2.2 ComfyUI failure is:

Trying to convert Float8_e4m3fn to the MPS backend but it does not have support for that dtype.

Source: ComfyUI issue #9255.

Experimental compatibility shims exist, such as ComfyUI-AppleSilicon-FP8, but this is not native FP8 execution. It routes conversions or substitutes Metal kernels and explicitly describes some paths as experimental.

GGUF

GGUF Q2/Q3 makes dual-14B Wan 2.2 physically loadable, but:

  • low-bit dequantization can be slow;
  • LoRA application can increase working memory;
  • VAE decoding can still OOM independently;
  • Q2 may damage motion/detail enough to compromise the test.

A community report on an M3 Max 36GB measured about 700 seconds for 41 Wan 2.2 frames using Q2, while 81 frames caused VAE memory failure. That is anecdotal rather than an official benchmark, but it is consistent with the expected memory boundary.

MLX

MLX is the better Apple-native execution layer. mlx-video supports:

  • Wan 2.1/2.2;
  • LTX-2/2.3;
  • quantized weights;
  • Wan 2.2 high/low LoRAs;
  • four-step Wan2.2-Lightning.

Its present missing feature is the conditioning interface needed for this task: SVI prev_samples, FLF endpoints, VACE temporal outpainting, or LTX keyframe interpolation.

A future MLX port of the SVI conditioning formula would likely be the best M3 solution, because the algorithm itself is simple compared with porting the full model. It is not currently an off-the-shelf method.

8. Acceleration compatibility

SVI

SVI is not a speed accelerator. It is a continuation/error-recycling LoRA and conditioning design. Normal denoising cost remains.

LightX2V / Wan2.2-Lightning

Official sources:

  • ModelTC/LightX2V
  • ModelTC/Wan2.2-Lightning
  • Wan2.2 Distill LoRAs

Wan 2.2 I2V requires matching high- and low-noise distillation LoRAs. Four total steps can work, though more often improves quality.

SVI Pro’s anchor redesign was explicitly intended to alleviate conflict with LightX2V. That does not mean every LightX2V version is validated. The SVI team still advises reducing LightX2V use when motion becomes slow and using 480p. Community tests report better long-run color stability with the Wan 2.2-specific LoRAs than using Wan 2.1 480p LoRAs at 720p.

Recommendation: establish the non-accelerated SVI result first. Then add one matched Wan 2.2 LightX2V high/low pair. Do not simultaneously add Lightning, CausVid, TeaCache, and alternate attention because the failure source becomes unknowable.

CausVid

Primary project: tianweiy/CausVid

Available Wan LoRAs are primarily based on Wan 2.1 T2V. They can reduce generation to roughly 4–12 steps, but are not an officially supported pair for Wan 2.2 SVI Pro’s two I2V experts.

Do not use a Wan2.1 CausVid LoRA as the primary SVI Pro accelerator unless accepting an unsupported experiment. It may weaken image/keyframe adherence and motion amplitude.

Attention and caching

Use PyTorch SDPA on the Mac.

Avoid assuming that SageAttention, FlashAttention, or TeaCache are lossless:

  • FlashAttention is CUDA-targeted.
  • SageAttention has community reports of SVI seam flashing.
  • FramePack’s author explicitly shows that TeaCache and quantization can materially alter outputs.

For final QA runs, disable cache approximations.

9. Concrete local test plan

Phase A: practical VACE baseline

  • Wan2.1-VACE-1.3B
  • 832×480
  • 41 frames first, then 81 if stable
  • FP16/BF16, not FP8
  • SDPA
  • 8 real overlap frames initially
  • next keyframe positioned at final frame
  • original VACE: 15–30 steps
  • disk-save each segment immediately

Test overlap values 5, 8, 12, and 16. Choose the smallest that preserves velocity without propagating blur.

Phase B: SVI Pro feasibility

  • Wan 2.2 I2V high/low Q2 or Q3 GGUF
  • matching SVI Pro high/low FP16 LoRAs
  • WanImageToVideoSVIProFLF
  • WanCutLastSlot(1)
  • 480p
  • 41 frames
  • motion_latent_count=1
  • five-frame decoded overlap trim
  • SDPA
  • unique seed per segment
  • no acceleration LoRA initially

If stable:

  1. increase to 81 frames;
  2. test motion_latent_count=2;
  3. test one matched LightX2V high/low pair;
  4. only then test longer sequences.

Phase C: hosted control

Run the same transition through Wan 2.7 at 720p using:

first_clip = preceding segment
last_frame = next keyframe
duration = input duration + intended continuation

Do not compare a local 480p Q2 output against Wan 2.7 solely on sharpness. Compare motion continuity and endpoint achievement separately.

10. Stitching and QA

Seam mechanics

For each seam retain:

  • the previous segment’s last 12–16 frames;
  • the next segment’s first 12–16 frames;
  • raw latents where available;
  • the exact overlap removed;
  • seed, prompt, model, LoRAs, and quantization.

Perform assembly in this order:

  1. remove deterministic duplicated overlap;
  2. inspect seam at full speed;
  3. inspect frame-by-frame;
  4. try ±1 frame trim;
  5. color-match only after temporal alignment;
  6. use optical-flow blending only as a last resort.

Recommended metrics

Primary evaluation suites:

  • VBench
  • EvalCrafter paper

Track:

  • subject consistency;
  • background consistency;
  • temporal flicker;
  • motion smoothness;
  • dynamic degree;
  • prompt/action consistency.

Add seam-specific measurements:

  1. Velocity jump
    Estimate optical flow before and after the seam. Compare median magnitude and direction. Normalize against ordinary within-segment variation.

  2. Seam warping error
    Warp the final pre-seam frame toward the first post-seam frame using optical flow and measure residual error.

  3. Keyframe adherence
    Compare generated endpoint against the requested keyframe using LPIPS plus DINO/CLIP similarity. Pixel SSIM alone over-penalizes valid texture changes.

  4. Identity drift
    DINO or face-embedding similarity from the original anchor to every segment endpoint.

  5. Color drift
    Compare Lab histogram/Delta-E across segment interiors and seams.

  6. Motion-collapse check
    Always report dynamic degree alongside consistency. A nearly static video can score deceptively well on flicker and identity.

  7. Human review
    Loop each seam three times at normal speed, then half speed. Rate:

    • trajectory continuity;
    • body/object deformation;
    • camera acceleration;
    • endpoint naturalness;
    • visible pause or reset.

Use relative acceptance thresholds: seam errors should fall within the median plus two standard deviations of ordinary internal frame transitions. This adapts to the motion intensity of each shot better than a universal LPIPS or flow cutoff.

Final recommendation

For this exact M3/36GB machine:

  • Use VACE 1.3B for a workflow you can realistically iterate locally.
  • Use SVI 2.0 Pro + FLF only as the high-value latent-continuation experiment, at 480p/Q2–Q3 and short windows.
  • Do not rely on FP8, block swap, or CUDA-specific attention to rescue the 14B stack on MPS.
  • Prefer MLX for ordinary Wan/LTX generation, but it does not yet expose the required continuation/keyframe controls.
  • Keep Wan 2.7 continuation as the paid reference implementation.
  • If the project becomes production-critical, an NVIDIA machine with at least 24GB VRAM—or rented 48GB+ GPU—is materially more suitable than the M3 Mac for SVI Pro, SkyReels V3, LongCat, or full LTX keyframe interpolation.
